newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Boeing makes new offer to win EU merger approval.
newsitem.headline: Boeing makes new offer to win EU merger approval.

text.p: Boeing Co made new proposals on Tuesday to win EU approval for its merger with McDonnell Douglas Corp as talks continued with the European Commission, a Boeing spokesman said.
"We have had discussions and we have continued to make proposals to try to find a mutually acceptable solution," Boeing's spokesman in Brussels, Craig Martin, told Reuters.

Martin declined to say whether the talks were finished or whether Boeing's offer was final. Boeing's vice-president for European affairs Jim Frank was equally elusive, but hinted that discussions may continue.
"I don't know what the word finished, final means," Frank said. He refused to elaborate on the latest talks.

Commission sources said at midday Boeing had only a few more hours to propose solutions to the executive's fears that the $14 billion merger would harm fair competition in the European civil aviation market.
The Commission had originally given the world's largest aircraft manufacturer until Monday night to make a new offer, but no agreement was reached despite night-long talks.

The Commission sources said it was crucial that the EU's competition concerns were met on Tuesday at the latest to allow for the consultation of national antitrust experts later this week before a final decision on July 23.
Boeing says the only deadline the Commission is bound to is July 31 -- when it completes its four-month in-depth investigation into the deal under the EU's merger control law.

Large multinationals have in the past proposed 11th hour concessions to win EU clearance for their merger plans. But European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert has warned that he has had enough of that.
"We cannot wait until the evening of the 22nd...today is the crucial day," one source said.
